layers_dropped.reason: analysis.frontend_components is empty. index.md: 'Backend only - no frontend, no container runtime.' The five components the feature passes inferred were dropped at merge; see merge_notes.

layers.name: Setup
layers.description: Create the Python project tree from scratch. No template: index.md's <rationale> disclaims one, so Layer 0 creates directories rather than copying a tree.

tasks.name: Project skeleton and dependency manifest
tasks.description: Create pyproject.toml declaring the project and its four runtime/test dependencies (fastapi 0.110+, sqlalchemy 2.x, pytest 8.x, httpx), a matching requirements.txt, and a .gitignore covering __pycache__, .pytest_cache and the SQLite database file. The target is an existing empty git repository -- do not run `git init`.
provides: Pinned dependency set including httpx for TestClient

tasks.name: Package layout and pytest configuration
tasks.description: Create the app and app.models packages and a pytest configuration that sets the test path and rootdir so `pytest` runs from the repository root.
provides: Runnable pytest with zero tests collected

tasks.name: SQLAlchemy engine, session, declarative Base and app instance
tasks.description: Create the file-backed SQLite engine, sessionmaker, declarative Base and a get_db dependency; a bare FastAPI application instance with no routes mounted; and a pytest conftest exposing an isolated per-test database session and a TestClient bound to it.

layers.name: Foundation
layers.description: The three declared data models. Link and Tag are independent of each other and run in parallel; LinkTag joins them.

tasks.name: Link model
tasks.description: Define the Link SQLAlchemy model exactly as save-link declares it: id integer pk, url text not null, title text null, created_at timestamp not null.

tasks.name: Tag model
tasks.description: Define the Tag SQLAlchemy model exactly as tag-links declares it: id integer pk, name text unique not null. Tag names are matched case-sensitively -- do not fold case.

tasks.name: LinkTag join table and Link-Tag association
tasks.description: Define the LinkTag association model (link_id fk Link.id, tag_id fk Tag.id, composite primary key over both) and add the many-to-many relationship attribute to the Link model. A join table is required explicitly by the feature: not a comma-separated string column.

layers.name: Backend
layers.description: Three endpoints, one router module each so no two tasks write the same file. Paths are unprefixed per merge_notes.

tasks.name: POST /links -- save a link
tasks.description: Pydantic request and response schemas for a link, and a POST /links route returning 201. url is required; title is optional and stored as null when absent, never derived from the page. A url that does not parse as an absolute http or https URL is rejected with 422 and nothing is stored.

tasks.name: GET /links -- list links, with optional tag filter
tasks.description: A GET /links route returning every stored link as a JSON array ordered most recently created first, empty when nothing is stored. An untitled link is reported with a null title rather than omitted. An optional ?tag= query parameter narrows the result to exactly the links carrying that tag. A failure to read the stored links returns 500 and never an empty array.

tasks.name: POST /links/{id}/tags -- attach tags to a link
tasks.description: A tag request schema and a POST /links/{id}/tags route returning 200 with the link reporting every attached tag. Re-posting a tag already attached leaves it attached exactly once. A link id that does not exist returns 404 and creates no tag rows. Do NOT implement any cleanup of tags left with no remaining links -- that decision is an open gap (tag-links#1) and inventing a policy for it is out of scope.

layers.name: Integration
layers.description: Mount the three routers and verify the save -> tag -> filtered-list path that crosses all three features and that no single feature task owns.

tasks.name: Mount routers and end-to-end flow test
tasks.description: Include the save_link, list_links and tag_links routers on the FastAPI application, create the schema at startup, and add an end-to-end test that saves two links, tags one of them, lists unfiltered to assert newest-first ordering across both, and lists filtered by tag to assert exactly the tagged link comes back.

notes.revision: Revised from the planner's first output. Four defects fixed: L0-001 carried 5 files against a 3-file limit; summary.total_tasks said 11 against 10 tasks; L2-001/002/003 all wrote app/api/links.py, which is a guaranteed collision in the merge queue; and the graph was fully linear, leaving no parallelism for the batch executor.
notes.parallelism: L2-002 and L2-003 are independent; one router module per endpoint task is what makes that pair independent. Layer 1 is deliberately sequential -- see shared_init_file.
notes.shared_init_file: L1-001, L1-002 and L1-003 each register their model in app/models/__init__.py, because tests/conftest.py runs `import app.models` before Base.metadata.create_all and an unregistered model has no table. That single file makes the three tasks unmergeable in parallel: they edit the same two lines from worktrees branched off the same base. Layer 1 was therefore serialised L1-001 -> L1-002 -> L1-003, and each task's requirement states the exact content it will find on disk and instructs an ADD to the import list rather than a rewrite. The parallelism given up is one round in a three-task layer; the merge conflict avoided would have halted the run.
notes.no_template: tech_stack.template.path is null. L0-001 creates the tree; there is no copy-template task and no git init -- the target is already an empty git repository.
notes.endpoint_paths: /links, /links/{id}/tags. Unprefixed. Two feature passes invented an /api prefix with nothing to read it from; only list-links#1 names a path in the PRD text, and it says GET /links.
notes.gap_not_resolved: tag-links#1 (decision, raised 2026-08-27): whether a tag with no remaining links is deleted or kept. L2-003 is instructed not to invent a policy. This gap blocks execution per core section 6 and is reported at the gate.
